The file is applied byte for byte: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.aws_tenant_partnership_consent_guard() (plpgsql, trigger, SET search_path = public, not SECURITY DEFINER), its COMMENT, REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC (EXECUTE for the owner only), DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS / CREATE TRIGGER aws_tenant_partnership_consent_guard BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON public.tenant_partnerships FOR EACH ROW, and DROP POLICY IF EXISTS of the five Supabase-era policies (Inviter can create partnerships, Partners can update partnerships, Admins can create any partnership, Admins can view any partnership, Admins can update any partnership). The guard trusts aws_connect_partner_by_code (SQL 32) by the sha256 of its three row writes and by its owner, so the engine also requires connect exactly as SQL 32 defines it (body sha256 1d8e36de…, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public, row_security=off: partnership_connect_pinned), owned by a role that is not checksops and that checksops is not a member of (partnership_connect_not_api_owned), and no other trigger on the table (tenant_partnerships_no_other_trigger). Prerequisites: tenant_partnerships with inviter_tenant_id, invitee_tenant_id, status and revoked_at; SQL 90's aws_user_tenant_ids() and aws_can_write_tenant(uuid); aws_connect_partner_by_code(text, uuid); auth.uid(); role checksops. No table, column, grant, other policy or row change; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin. Adds one trigger (the DB validator already requires it).
